extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced students (algebraists, geometers, analysts) interested in foundational problems across algebra, geometry, analysis, and the calculus of variations
extracted.subtask_description: A broad scholarly lecture enumerating and formulating open mathematical problems and precise definitions across algebraic functions, topology of algebraic curves/surfaces, variational calculus, PDE boundary problems, uniformization, and related areas. It states exact conditions/definitions and poses questions about existence, representation, and structural finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'relativganze Function' (relatively integral function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eine rationale Function von X1,...,Xm heißt relativganze, wenn sie nach Ausführung der Substitution (S) ganz in x1,...,xn wird.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes observation that every whole (ganze) function in X1,...,Xm is relativganze; sums, differences, and products of relativganze functions are relativganze. This is the class whose finiteness-properties are investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endlicher Integritätsbereich (finite integrality domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ein System von Funktionen heißt endlicher Integritätsbereich, wenn sich aus ihm eine endliche Anzahl von Funktionen auswählen läßt, mit deren Hilfe alle übrigen Funktionen des Systems in ganzer rationaler Weise ausdrückbar sind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principal problem: show that all relativganzen functions of any rationality domain form such a finite integrality domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number-theoretic refinement for integer coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Refinement: take coefficients of f1,...,fm to be whole rational integers and consider only those relativganzen rational functions which after substitution (S) become whole rational functions in x1,...,xn with integer coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads to special cases and questions about finiteness when restricting coefficient domains (integers) and denominator powers (p^h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness for p-adic denominators (special case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given X1,...,Xm rational functions of a single variable x with integer coefficients and a prime p, consider functions of the form G(X1,...,Xm)/p^h (G integral) — previous work shows all such expressions for a fixed exponent h form a finite integrality domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question raised: does a single finite generating set exist that simultaneously represents all such expressions for all exponents h?

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous foundation of Schubert's enumerative calculus
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove rigorously the geometric enumerative numbers obtained by Schubert via the 'principle of special position' and his counting calculus, with precise determination of validity limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires elimination carried out for specially shaped equations so that degree of final equations and multiplicity of solutions can be predicted; more than abstract elimination existence is needed for concrete counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topology of algebraic curves: arrangement beyond Harnack's bound
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the mutual disposition (gegenseitige Lage) of ovals (Züge) of a plane algebraic curve attaining Harnack's maximal number of ovals; e.g., for sextic curves determine possible arrangements of the 11 ovals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate not just counts (Harnack) but placements, nesting structures, and which configurations are impossible or necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topology of algebraic surfaces: maximum number and arrangement of 'Mäntel'
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the maximal number, shape and arrangement of the 'shells' (Mäntel) of an algebraic surface in space — e.g., unknown maximum number of shells for a quartic surface in three-dimensional space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous questions to planar curves but in spatial setting; important open enumerative/topological problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal number and location of Poincaré limit cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the maximal number and mutual arrangement of Poincaré limit cycles (cycles limites) for first-order ODEs dy/dx = Y/X where X,Y are whole rational functions of degree n in x,y (or their homogeneous form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the qualitative/dynamical question: count limit cycles and understand possible configurations for polynomial vector fields of given degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of definite forms by sums of squares / quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: A definite (definit) whole rational form (real coefficients, never negative) — question whether every definite form can be represented as a quotient of sums of squares of forms (or expressed by sums of square-forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted: every square is definite, but not every definite form is a sum of squares; the problem asks about representation as quotient of sums of squares, with positive results in certain ternary cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality of coefficients in representation of definite forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When representing a definite form as quotient (or sum) of squares, can the coefficients of the representing forms be taken in the same rationality domain as those of the represented form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question relevant for constructive and arithmetic aspects of representations; important for geometric construction questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of motion groups with fundamental domains in different geometries
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate which motion groups (Bewegungsgruppen) admit a fundamental region (Fundamentalbereich) in elliptic (Riemannian), Euclidean, and hyperbolic planes/spaces; note finiteness contrasts: elliptic finite types, hyperbolic infinite types, Euclidean finite types but infinite number of copies needed to tile space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In higher dimensions ask whether there are only finitely many essentially different types of motion groups with fundamental domain (analogue of Rohn, Fedorow, Schoenflies results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of polyhedra that tile space but are not fundamental domains of groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Do there exist polyhedra which are not fundamental regions of any motion group but nonetheless tile space by congruent copies (suitable packings) to fill space without gaps?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to packing/tiling questions and to number-theoretic/physical applications; investigate existence and construction methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Densest packing (Einbetten) of congruent bodies in space
rubrics_metrics.description: How to embed (lager) infinitely many congruent bodies (e.g., spheres of given radius or regular tetrahedra of given edge/position) in space so that the ratio of filled to unfilled space is as large as possible (sphere-packing/packing density problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses densest packings for various shapes; both geometric and number-theoretic significance, with applications in physics/chemistry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality of analytic functions as class for study
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal: the class of analytic functions is the natural central class for function theory — it includes functions from number theory, differential equations, algebraic functional equations, geometry, and mathematical physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that narrower classes (algebraic-differential functions) omit important arithmetic examples (ζ(s)), while too broad smooth classes lose analytic continuation and power series tools; justifies analytic class as balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'regular' variational problem (ellipticity & analyticity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Call a variational problem regular if F(p,q,z;x,y) is analytic and satisfies the inequality F_pp * F_qq - (F_pq)^2 > 0 for all admissible arguments (ellipticity condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regularity underlies the question whether solutions of such variational problems must necessarily be analytic functions of the independent variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are solutions of regular variational problems necessarily analytic?
rubrics_metrics.description: Question: Do Lagrange partial differential equations coming from regular variational problems admit only analytic integrals (solutions), even with merely continuous non-analytic boundary values?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations: some PDEs (potential equation, certain Picard linear equations, minimal surface PDE) force analyticity; yet counterexamples exist in differential geometry (surfaces of negative curvature). Investigate general analytic regularity results.

rubrics_metrics.name: General boundary value problem existence criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish existence of solutions to PDEs with prescribed boundary conditions beyond classical potential theory: include cases with prescribed derivative boundary data or boundary conditions for non-potential variational problems (e.g., minimal surfaces, constant positive curvature surfaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjecture that existence follows from general principles (Dirichlet principle-like) under assumptions such as continuity and piecewise higher differentiability of boundary data and possibly broadened notion of solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of linear differential equations with prescribed monodromy (Riemann–Hilbert type problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that for given singular points and a given monodromy group there exists a linear differential equation of the Fuchsian class realizing those singularities and that monodromy (i.e., n functions regular except at given singularities, with prescribed linear substitutions upon analytic continuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known proofs exist in special cases (eigenvalues of monodromy of modulus 1 via Schlesinger using Poincaré theory of Fuchsian ζ-functions); general existence remains open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformization of analytic relations by automorphic functions (coverage of all regular points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalize Poincaré's uniformization: for arbitrary analytic (not only algebraic) relations between two variables, find automorphic functions that uniformize the relation and determine whether these can be chosen so that while the new variable ranges over its regular domain all regular points of the original analytic object are represented (i.e., no essential discrete exceptional points except branch points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also raises uniformization questions in three or more complex variables; existing work of Picard on two-variable algebraic functions is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass and Jacobi conditions for minima in calculus of variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive necessary and sufficient criteria for a functional minimum: use independence of the constructed integral J* from path to obtain PDEs for p(x,y), leading to Weierstrass' expression E(y_x,p)=F(y_x)-F(p)-(y_x-p)F_p(p) and the conditions E>0 (Weierstrass condition) together with the Jacobi condition for sufficiency/necessity of a minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulas and arguments generalize to multiple dependent variables and multiple integrals; use polar process and characteristic relations between second-order Euler–Lagrange equations and first-order PDEs for p to establish conditions.
